title: Hydride superconductor pressure barrier
bottleneck: The highest confirmed superconducting transition temperatures, around 203-250 K in sulfur hydride and lanthanum hydride, require pressures above 150 GPa. No known mechanism yet explains how to retain hydride-like electron-phonon coupling at ambient pressure, and attempts to stabilize hydrides with chemical pre-compression have only shaved fractions off the required pressure. The ternary candidate LaSc2H24, reported in 2025 with Tc up to 298 K, still needs about 250 GPa.
why_it_blocks: Pressure is the deal-breaker: diamond anvil cells produce microgram samples, so hydride results cannot be scaled into wires, magnets, or devices. Until high-Tc physics survives at ambient pressure, these materials remain scientific milestones with no engineering path.
current_state: Researchers are hunting boron-based compounds and new ternary hydrides at lower pressures, but as one physicist noted in 2026, a consumer-usable ambient superconductor is unlikely within 10-15 years. Near-term progress is expected in nitrogen-cooled high-temperature superconductors for grids instead.

sources.title: How Close Are We to Superconductors That Are Actually Practical?
